At.description: Where a finding is reported. Every field is a CEL expression.

endLine.description: The last line, for a finding about a file.

line.description: The first line, for a finding about a file.

symbol.description: The id of a symbol: the finding is reported at that symbol and cites it.

Batch.description: How a `command` check batches the files it is given.

oneOf.description: One run per file.

Runs over many files at once, as many per run as the argument list
allows; `{files}` expands to several arguments.

name.description: A lower-case identifier that no expression variable already uses.

BuiltinCheck.description:
A builtin check: one of the standard, decision-agnostic operations, or a
rule registered by name that no standard operation can express.

BuiltinOp.description: A standard operation over the code model.

oneOf.description:
Declarations must follow the order of registered order keys, the same
keys a `reorder` fix sorts by. Each clause is judged on its own and the
findings are concatenated.

Declarations that belong together stay together: nothing but members
of the same `group` may separate two of them.

contiguous.description:
The group is contiguous: no separator at all. The default when
`maxDistance` is not given.

evidence.description: Evidence fields, each a CEL expression over the same variables.

group.description:
CEL over a declaration (`symbol`) that gives the key of the group
it belongs to; empty when it belongs to none.

maxDistance.description:
How many separating declarations a group tolerates between two of
its members.

message.description:
Text over `symbol` (the member separated from the group),
`previous` (the member before it), `separators` (the declarations
between, as a list), `count` and `options`.

separator.description:
CEL over `between`, a declaration lying between two members of the
group, and `member` (the later one) and `key` (the group's key):
true for a declaration that splits the group. Default: any
declaration that is not in the group.

when.description: CEL over `file`: the check runs on the files it is true for.

oneOf.description: No dependency cycle over edges of one kind.

Capability.description: Provider feature that rules may require.

oneOf.description: Symbols carry an [`Symbol::extent`]: the full declaration range.
Edges carry the [`Edge::site`] where the reference occurs.

Every reference to a symbol is an edge with a site: signatures, fields
and receivers included, so a rename cannot miss one.

The provider analyzes the `overlays` of an index request instead of the
files on disk; a fix needs it to verify an edit before writing it.

Check.description:
How a decision is checked, mirroring [`crate::Fix`]: one provider selected by
`type`, with the fields every provider shares. Which other fields a check
may have depends on its `type`; any other is refused.

oneOf.description: A standard operation, or a rule registered by a bundled plugin.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: A CEL expression over the code model.

at.description: Where the finding is reported when it is not at the selected value.

evidence.description: Evidence fields, each a CEL expression.

identity.description:
What makes a finding the same finding from one run to the next, when
the default (the selected value) does not.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

select.description:
What the check looks at. Default: what the decision's `scope.subject`
is about; a decision about the project says which it looks at.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

with.description:
Named intermediate values, evaluated in order before `where`; each
expression sees the ones before it.

oneOf.description: An external program under the process contract.

argv.description:
Program and arguments; `{file}`, `{files}` and `{rule}` fill whole
arguments.

columns.description:
The unit the program counts columns in, when its log does not say or
says wrongly; only with `output: sarif`. Default: the log's
`columnKind`, else `utf16CodeUnits`.

output.description:
How stdout is read when the program found something: one finding per
line (default), or a SARIF 2.1.0 log.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

select.description: Which SARIF results become findings; only with `output: sarif`.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: A language plugin's check method. Reserved until protocol 0.2.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description:
Agent review: a model is asked about the candidates. Not
deterministic; today's agent review tasks serve it.

prompt.description: What the model is told. Default: the decision's requirement.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

select.description:
CEL over the code model that picks the subjects worth asking about.
Default: the subjects that match the decision's scope.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

requires.description:
Capabilities the language provider must offer; without them the check
is not run for that language.

timeout.description: How long one run of the provider may take, such as `30s` or `2m`.

CheckOutput.description: How a `command` check reads what the program printed.

oneOf.description: One finding per line, with an optional `path:line[:col]: ` prefix.
A SARIF 2.1.0 log: one finding per result.

CheckStdin.description: What a `command` check gives the program on stdin.

oneOf.description: The content of the file (only with `batch: file`).

CommandOutput.description: What the orchestrator takes from a command that succeeded.

oneOf.description: The command edits the scratch copy of the file.
The command prints the new text of the file on stdout, and nothing else.

CommandScope.description: Where a command's edits may land.

oneOf.description: Only the finding's file.

CommandStdin.description: What the command is given on stdin.

oneOf.description: The content of the target file.

CycleLevel.description: At what level a `cycle` check looks for strongly connected components.

DecisionSpec.description:
A design decision, the way an architecture decision record states one:
what was decided and why, its status, and how it is enforced. The engine
compiles `check` into the rule that enforces it. A decision without a
`check` is documentation only.

consequences.description: What follows from the decision, good and bad.

context.description:
Why the decision exists: the forces at play, as an architecture
decision record's context states them.

fix.description:
How the findings of the rule are fixed; the catalog is the one place
that says.

languages.description: What each language changes: option values and wording, by language id.

options.description: Tunable values, as a JSON Schema object.

requirement.description: What the decision demands, in RFC 2119 words.

severity.description:
The severity of the decision's findings, as authored. `error` is
definitive: it needs no review and only a directive in the code
waives it, and its fix may be safe. `warn` and `info` are review
tasks: a reviewer's judgment may hide them and a fix is at most
suggested. A decision without a `check` has none. A configuration
`level` changes what is reported and the exit code, never this.

status.description: Where the decision stands: only an accepted one is enforced.

supersedes.description: The decisions this one replaces, by id. Each becomes `superseded`.

DecisionStatus.description:
Where a decision stands in its life, as an architecture decision record
does. Only an accepted decision is enforced.

oneOf.description: Under discussion: written down, not yet enforced.
Considered and turned down; kept so the question is not asked again.
Replaced by another decision (named in that decision's `supersedes`).
No longer wanted, and nothing replaces it.

Domain.description:
What kind of thing a decision is about: source code, or Lighthouse's own
documents (the decisions of a catalog).

oneOf.description: The documents of a project that configure Lighthouse.

Example.description:
A fixture project for one language and what a rule must report on it:
nothing for `valid`, the diagnostics of `expect` for `invalid`.

canonical.description:
The example that best shows the decision in its language; at most one
per language and kind. Agent output prefers it.

expect.description: Diagnostics an invalid example must produce.

fixed.description:
What an invalid example's files become when the decision's fix is
applied: the files that change, each with its whole new text. Applying
the fix again must change nothing, and the rule must no longer fire.

options.description: Rule options the example runs with.

ExampleFile.description:
One file of an example project, addressed by `path` inside the example.
Its text is a `body` written in the decision file, or a `source` file next
to it.

ExampleKind.description:
Whether an example must produce no diagnostics (`valid`) or exactly those
listed in `expect` (`invalid`).

ExitCodes.description:
Which exit codes mean what; every other code, a signal or a timeout is an
error and leaves the analysis incomplete.

Expect.description: An expected diagnostic of an invalid example.

Fix.description:
How a decision's findings are fixed and how far the fix may be trusted.
Which fields a fix may have depends on its `type`; any other is refused.

oneOf.description: Generic operations over the code model, evaluated with CEL.

requires.description: Provider capabilities the fix needs; without them it is declined.

safety.description:
Caps what the fixer may claim: a `safe` proposal under a `suggested`
decision is downgraded. `safe` is reserved for decisions that author `error`.

oneOf.description: An external program on a scratch copy of the files.

argv.description:
Program and arguments; `{file}`, `{line}`, `{symbol}` and `{rule}` fill
whole arguments.

requires.description: Provider capabilities the fix needs; without them it is declined.

safety.description:
Caps what the fixer may claim: a `safe` proposal under a `suggested`
decision is downgraded. `safe` is reserved for decisions that author `error`.

timeout.description: How long it may run, such as `30s` or `2m`.

oneOf.description: A language plugin's fix method. Reserved: not yet supported.

requires.description: Provider capabilities the fix needs; without them it is declined.

safety.description:
Caps what the fixer may claim: a `safe` proposal under a `suggested`
decision is downgraded. `safe` is reserved for decisions that author `error`.

requires.description: Provider capabilities the fix needs; without them it is declined.

safety.description:
Caps what the fixer may claim: a `safe` proposal under a `suggested`
decision is downgraded. `safe` is reserved for decisions that author `error`.

Identity.description:
The identity of a finding: its fingerprint is a hash of the decision, the
`subject` and the whitespace-normalized `snippet`. Both are CEL expressions
that give text.

LanguageSpec.description: What one language changes about a decision: the values of its options.

options.description: Values of the decision's options that replace their defaults here.

Metadata.description:
Who a resource is. Identity is `name`; grouping is by label, never by
where the document is stored.

annotations.description: Free notes; never used to select.

uid.description:
Identity that outlives the name: a UUID v4 assigned once, never derived
from the name (Kubernetes `metadata.uid`). Renaming a resource keeps it.

NamedRule.description:
A rule implemented in Rust and registered by a bundled plugin. Strays are
refused by [`Check`], which knows the fields every provider shares.

id.description: The id of the registered rule.

ObjectType.description: The only `type` of the options object.

OpSpec.description:
One operation of an `ops` fix. Every parameter but `scope` and `by` is a
CEL expression over the finding (`finding`, `symbol`, `options`) or, for
`text` and `name`, a template with `{{ cel }}` holes. A `when` expression
that is false skips the operation.

OptionSchema.description:
One tunable value: its shape, default and description. The shape's keys
sit beside `default` and `description`; a key that is none of them is
refused.

OptionsSchema.description:
A JSON Schema object that declares the options of a decision. Keys not
declared are refused: `additionalProperties` is `false`.

OrderClause.description: One ordering a container of declarations must follow.

by.description: Qualified `plugin/name` order keys, most significant first.

evidence.description: Evidence fields, each a CEL expression over the same variables.

message.description:
Text with `{{ cel }}` holes over `symbol` (the declaration reported),
`rank` and `ranks` (its rank by the first key and by every key),
`after` (with `displaced`: the declaration it must follow, else an
empty node), `earlier` (with `late`: the first declaration before it
that ranks higher) and `options`.

when.description:
CEL over `file` and `options`: the clause runs on the files it is
true for. Default: every file.

within.description: What is ordered: each module of a file, or each owner's members.

OrderReport.description: How an `order` clause picks the declarations to report.

oneOf.description:
The fewest declarations that, moved, would put the container in order:
those outside its longest in-order run.
Every declaration that has an earlier one of a higher rank.
Every declaration of a file, each module on its own.
Only the members of one owner.

Provenance.description: Where a decision comes from, in the vocabulary of W3C PROV.

wasDerivedFrom.description:
The sources the decision was derived from: a paper, a tool's rule, the
lines of a document it covers.

oneOf.description: Every declaration of the finding's file, each container sorted on its own.
Only the members of the finding symbol's owner.

Safety.description: How much a proposed fix may be trusted to keep the program's meaning.

oneOf.description: Mechanical and meaning-preserving: applied by default.
Probably right but a judgment call: applied only when asked for.

SarifColumns.description:
The unit a SARIF log counts columns in (`columnKind`, plus the bytes that
tools such as golangci-lint count without saying so).

oneOf.description: UTF-16 code units.
Unicode code points.
Bytes.

SarifSelect.description:
The results of a SARIF log that become findings; a result must pass both
lists. This `select` is a field of the command check, not the CEL `select`
of other checks.

levels.description:
SARIF `level`s to keep: `error`, `warning`, `note` or `none`; a result
without a level is a `warning`. Default: every level.

ruleIds.description:
Globs over the result's `ruleId`, such as `errcheck` or `govet:*`: `*`
is any run of characters inside one segment, segments being separated
by `/` or `::`, and `**` is any number of segments, as in module path
globs. Default: every rule.

Scope.description:
Where a decision applies: its domain, what it is about, and which code its
subjects may be in. Generated and test code are told apart by the host
(the provider's marker, `.gitattributes`, the project's `generated`
globs), and the engine leaves the subjects out that the scope excludes
before any check runs.

generated.description: Generated code is a subject too. Default: it is not.

tests.description:
Which test code is a subject: `exclude` (the default), `include` or
`only`.

Select.description: What a CEL check looks at; each choice binds one variable of the same name.

oneOf.description: A comment of a file, with its text and position.

A body event of a function (a panic, an `unwrap`, an error compared
with `==`, ...): one finding per event, at the event. The event has
its `kind`, `detail`, `line` and the function it is in (`event.func`).

A decision document of the project: its name, pack, labels and kind,
and where it is written.

Severity.description:
How hard a finding fails a run; serialized and parsed as the lowercase
variant name. Whether a finding also asks for review is not a level: it
follows from the severity its decision authored.

oneOf.description: Fails the run.
Fails the run only under `--strict` or past `--max-warnings`.
Reported, never fails the run.

Subject.description:
What a decision talks about inside its domain. Mapping to the run scope
of a rule is `Subject::run_scope`.

oneOf.description: A relation between two symbols or modules, such as an import.
A decision document, in the `spec` domain.

TestScope.description: Which test code a decision applies to.

oneOf.description: Production code only.
Production and test code.
Test code only.
